225—234. Stichomythia and conclusion, the latter in twice three verses, just as at 198 three verses stood at the beginning.

226 ⟦1⟧ different from ⟦2⟧: the words of the other speaker create the contrast, cf. (Sidgwick) ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ ("that is all the same to me, as far as I am concerned"; thus likewise breaking off the discussion). Paley also compares Eurip. '⟦5⟧. ⟦6⟧. 726. ⟦7⟧.

227 f.: the Erinyes see a curtailment of their office in it, if all their trouble is to be in vain. Curtail? Apollo replies; I want nothing of your honors. Then they: of course you are great, despite me, under this new regime.

The ⟦5⟧ transmitted only here in Aeschylus is corrected by Porson to ⟦6⟧; it is hard to say whether the aversion to the tribrach was greater or that to the non-Attic form, since ⟦7⟧ (79) is not avoided even in the trimeter. In such matters one does best to follow the tradition. Cf. on 243. Also at 231 apocope seems to be transmitted, if in ⟦8⟧ (M) Wellauer's ⟦9⟧ is concealed; however, this would not be acceptable for several reasons, and ⟦10⟧ (Erfurdt) is likely correct. ⟦11⟧ also has ⟦12⟧ (⟦13⟧), ⟦14⟧ no one; also in its formation ⟦15⟧ is somewhat strange. Furthermore, the parallelism with 232 demands a second verb here, and it would be wrong to think that this must be a future because ⟦16⟧ is one. Rather, this is a real present like ⟦17⟧ 242 (see below), and denotes what is already happening; for with this verse (consisting of pure iambs) the chorus hurries away. At the end of the verse, however, where writing was often smaller and less clear, something like a misreading of -⟦18⟧ as THC is possible. ⟦19⟧ like ⟦20⟧ ⟦21⟧ (similarly there 345, Paley).
